_comment: Known-good decode configs per machine. Throughput is NOT monotonic in batch size, so these are measured, not calculated. Add yours: run `mlx-asr-bench` and open an issue with its output. Keys are matched as substrings of `sysctl -n machdep.cpu.brand_string` plus a RAM window in nameplate GiB. Machines with no entry fall through to a derived formula (see hardware.py: derive_batch), not to a bucket table.

_schema.batch: rows decoded in lockstep; the single most important knob
_schema.chunk_seconds: audio per row; shorter = fewer decode steps per row but more chunk seams. 30s vs 60s is not resolvable on the 20-file corpus (+0.10, CI [-1.89, +2.03]), so this is a throughput choice, not an accuracy one
_schema.measured_x_realtime: end-to-end on the reference clip, incl. model load
_schema.peak_gb: GPU peak at this batch; keep under ~60% of gpu_working_set_gb
_schema.source: who measured it and on what
_schema.ram_gb: nameplate GiB, i.e. the number on the spec sheet (a 16GB Mac reports 16, not 17)
_schema.model_id: e.g. Mac16,1: the enclosure, and therefore the cooling class. Chip and RAM do not determine sustained throughput; a fanless Air, a MacBook Pro and a Mac Studio with the same chip hold different clocks over a minutes-long decode. Recorded for provenance, not matched on, until two profiles disagree at equal chip+RAM

profiles.notes: 10 GPU cores, ~120GB/s. 60s/B16 because SHORTER chunks lose here: the encoder is 36% of wall clock and compute-bound, so doubling the chunk count costs more than the shorter decode rows save. Measured 30s/B32 slower than 60s/B16 on this chip, which is the opposite of the M2 Ultra and the reason chunk length is a profile value rather than a flag. B=4..8 is a hard valley (110ms/step vs 22ms at B=1) and B=48 exceeds the ~8.4GB KV wall. Overlap stays 0: it won 1.8 CER points at 30s on one clip and did not reproduce on the 20-file corpus.
profiles.source: Apple M4, 16GB, 10 GPU cores (Mac16,1), mlx 0.32.0, nvfp4

profiles.notes: 60 GPU cores, ~800GB/s. 30s/B32 measured 28.9x against 19.8x for 60s/B16 over the 20-file corpus at identical accuracy (16.22% vs 16.21%, paired -0.01 CI [-1.96, +1.87]), so short chunks are a free 46% here. That is the reverse of the low-core M4, where the same change loses. Overlap stays 0: adding 8s cost both speed and accuracy on this corpus (23.5x at 16.79%). A whole 935s clip fits in one batch of 32, so nothing is lost to padding.
profiles.source: Apple M2 Ultra, 128GB, 60 GPU cores (Mac14,14), mlx 0.32.0, 4bit affine, 20-file corpus

derived._comment: Inputs to hardware.py:derive_batch, used only when no profile above matches. Batch itself is computed from GPU working set, GPU cores, model weight size and chunk length, then snapped onto FAST_BATCHES; it is deliberately NOT a table, because memory and core count are detectable at runtime while the batch-size valley is not.
derived._chunk_note: 60s both ways for now. On a low-core GPU the compute-bound encoder makes short chunks a net loss on throughput; that is measured on the M4 but not yet on any other low-core part, so the two values are kept separate rather than collapsed. This is a speed argument, not an accuracy one: 30s and 60s are indistinguishable on accuracy over the 20-file corpus.
